water_notes: Allow the top 2 inches of soil to dry out between waterings. Reduce in winter.
soil: Chunky, well-draining aroid mix with orchid bark, perlite, and coco peat.
fertilizer: Balanced 20-20-20 liquid fertilizer monthly during spring and summer.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to cats and dogs (calcium oxalate crystals)
toxicity_humans: Mildly toxic; irritates mouth and throat if chewed raw
growth_notes: Provides aerial roots. Attach to a coir or moss pole to support upright climbing and larger fenestrated leaves.
fun_fact: The natural perforations in leaves (fenestrations) allow hurricane winds to pass through in tropical rainforests without tearing the leaf.

light: Low light to bright direct sun (highly adaptable)
water_notes: Water only when the potting mix is bone dry down to the bottom. Never let water stand in rosette.
soil: Cactus/succulent gritty soil with coarse sand and pumice.
fertilizer: Half-strength cactus fertilizer twice a year in spring/summer.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to dogs and cats (saponins)
growth_notes: Extremely drought-tolerant. Rhizomes multiply readily and can gently crack plastic nursery pots when rootbound.
fun_fact: One of the few plants that releases oxygen at night through Crassulacean Acid Metabolism (CAM), making it an ideal bedroom plant.

light: Medium to bright indirect light (tolerates low light)
water_notes: Water when top 1 inch of soil is dry. Can also grow indefinitely in a glass bottle of clean water.
soil: Standard rich, well-draining indoor potting mix.
fertilizer: Dilute nitrogen-rich fertilizer every 3 weeks during summer.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to pets due to insoluble calcium oxalates
growth_notes: Vigorous cascading climber. Snip vines right below a root node to propagate roots in water within 10 days.
fun_fact: In Vastu Shastra and Feng Shui, keeping a money plant in the Southeast corner of the home is believed to attract positive energy and prosperity.

light: Low light to medium filtered light
water_notes: Stores water in potato-like underground rhizomes. Water thoroughly once every 2-3 weeks; do not overwater.
soil: Well-draining potting soil with perlite.
fertilizer: Quarter-strength balanced fertilizer once in spring.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to pets
growth_notes: Natural glossy waxy foliage that looks polished without leaf shine spray. Thrives even in windowless offices under fluorescent lights.
fun_fact: Can survive without water for months by shedding its leaflets and retreating into its subterranean tuberous rhizomes.

light: Medium indirect light to deep shade
water_notes: Keep soil lightly moist. Dramatically wilts when thirsty and bounds back within hours after watering.
soil: Peat-based moisture-retentive potting mix with vermiculite.
fertilizer: Mild blooming fertilizer every 6 weeks during flowering.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to dogs and cats
growth_notes: The white 'flower' is actually a specialized leaf bract called a spathe sheltering a spadix of tiny blossoms.
fun_fact: Ranked among top air-purifying indoor plants in the famous NASA Clean Air Study for removing benzene and formaldehyde.

water_notes: Allow soil to dry out completely. Water deeply until liquid drains from bottom, then discard runoff.
soil: Sandy, porous cactus and succulent potting mix.
fertilizer: Rarely needed; dilute organic fertilizer in spring.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to pets (aloin causes digestive upset)
toxicity_humans: Gel is non-toxic externally; latex layer under skin is laxative
growth_notes: Pups (offshoots) emerge around mother rosette; separate and repot into individual terracotta containers.
fun_fact: Revered in Ayurvedic medicine for thousands of years as 'Kumari', renowned for soothing thermal skin burns and minor cuts.

light: Bright, consistent indirect sunlight near an east or south window
water_notes: Water thoroughly when top 2 inches dry out. Prone to root edema from standing water.
soil: Rich, well-aerated potting mix with perlite and pine bark.
fertilizer: High-nitrogen liquid houseplant fertilizer once a month in active growth.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to dogs and cats
toxicity_humans: Milky sap can cause dermal irritation
growth_notes: Dislikes sudden relocation or drafts. Wipe dust from large leaves once every 2 weeks to maximize sunlight intake.
fun_fact: In its native West African tropical rainforest habitat, it can reach over 50 feet tall and starts life as an epiphyte in tree crowns.

water_notes: Allow upper third of potting mix to dry before re-watering.
soil: Aerated well-draining loamy potting soil.
fertilizer: Monthly balanced liquid plant food in spring/summer.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to pets
toxicity_humans: Milky latex sap irritates skin and eyes
growth_notes: Thick glossy burgundy-green leaves. In Northeast India (Meghalaya), the living roots of this species are trained over centuries into living root bridges.
fun_fact: The ancient Khasi tribes engineered living suspension bridges across surging rivers using living aerial roots of Ficus elastica.

light: Bright indirect to light partial shade
water_notes: Water evenly when top inch is dry. Use filtered water if leaf tips turn brown from fluoride.
soil: Well-draining general potting mix.
fertilizer: Balanced houseplant food once every 4 weeks in summer.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic (pet-safe!)
growth_notes: Sends out cascading runners bearing white star flowers and miniature 'spiderettes' ready for propagation.
fun_fact: Cats are mildly attracted to spider plants because the foliage contains mild hallucinogenic compounds similar to catnip.

light: Gentle morning sun or dappled shade; never direct harsh sun
water_notes: Keep soil consistently damp like a wrung-out sponge. Mist fronds regularly.
soil: Peat-rich, spongy soil mixed with compost and perlite.
fertilizer: Weak water-soluble fertilizer every month.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic and 100% pet-safe
growth_notes: Loves high-humidity spaces like well-lit bathrooms. Prune dry outer fronds at the soil crown.
fun_fact: A staple of Victorian parlor gardens since the late 1800s, praised for its lush gracefully arching emerald fronds.

water_notes: Allow the top inch to dry between waterings. Sensitive to tap water chlorine.
soil: Loamy soil rich in peat with good bottom drainage.
fertilizer: Slow-release micronutrient palm fertilizer in spring.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic and pet friendly
growth_notes: Clumping palm with graceful feather-like fronds. Naturally humidifies dry indoor air by transpiring up to 1 liter of water daily.
fun_fact: Acts as a potent natural humidifier, transpirating nearly a quart of clean moisture into the surrounding air every 24 hours.

light: At least 4-6 hours of direct bright sunlight daily
water_notes: Soak deeply only when fleshy oval leaves begin to feel slightly soft or wrinkled.
soil: Fast-draining gritty succulent mix with pumice, gravel, and coarse sand.
fertilizer: Quarter-strength balanced feed every 2 months in summer.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to dogs and cats
growth_notes: Develops a thick woody bonsai-like trunk with age. Can live for over 50 years with minimal care.
fun_fact: Commonly placed near the entrances of shops and homes in Asian folklore to welcome prosperity, success, and good luck.

light: Medium to bright indirect light; direct sun burns colorful leaves
water_notes: Strictly use distilled, rainwater, or RO water. Sensitive to tap fluoride and salts.
soil: Moisture-retentive airy blend of peat, perlite, and worm castings.
fertilizer: Weak half-strength nitrogen fertilizer once a month.
toxicity_pets: 100% Non-toxic and pet safe
growth_notes: Practices nyctinasty: leaves fold upward together at night like praying hands and unfurl outward during the day.
fun_fact: The leaves fold upright each evening as if in solemn prayer, a circadian rhythm mechanism known as nyctinasty.

water_notes: Water thoroughly when top half of substrate is dry. Do not let roots sit in waterlogged soil.
soil: Very chunky orchid bark and coarse peat moss.
fertilizer: High-phosphorus orchid fertilizer every 6 weeks to promote glossy spathes.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to pets
growth_notes: The glossy red heart-shaped structure is a modified waxy spathe with a flower-bearing spadix.
fun_fact: Known as the world's longest-blooming houseplant; each vibrant waxy heart-shaped spathe can endure for up to 8 weeks.

water_notes: Water once every 7-10 days when top 2 inches dry.
soil: Standard peat-based potting soil with good aeration.
fertilizer: Slow-release pellets once in spring.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to pets
growth_notes: Remarkably resilient houseplant featuring variegated silver, pink, or red patterned foliage.
fun_fact: Regarded as a lucky charm in Asian culture, historically cultivated in royal gardens for hundreds of years.

common_name: Holy Basil (Tulsi / Krishna Tulsi / Rama Tulsi)
light: Full direct sunlight (at least 6 hours daily)
water_notes: Water daily in warm Indian summers; keep soil moist but never waterlogged. Reduce in winter.
soil: Fertile, loamy, well-draining garden soil enriched with vermicompost.
fertilizer: Monthly compost tea, cow dung manure, or organic seaweed extract.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic and safe for animals
toxicity_humans: Non-toxic; widely consumed as sacred medicinal herbal tea
growth_notes: Pinch off flowering seed tips (manjari) regularly to encourage bushy, dense aromatic leaf growth.
fun_fact: Considered sacred in Hinduism as an avatar of Goddess Lakshmi. Scientific studies confirm its powerful adaptogenic and antimicrobial properties.

water_notes: Drought-tolerant once established. Young saplings need deep watering once or twice a week.
soil: Thrives in all soil types including dry stony sandy soils; requires good subsoil drainage.
fertilizer: Farmyard manure once a year before monsoon.
toxicity_pets: Neem oil in high concentration is toxic to cats; whole leaves mildly toxic in excess
toxicity_humans: Bark and leaves medicinal; pure neem oil is toxic if swallowed
growth_notes: Fast-growing evergreen tree reaching 50-65 feet. Excellent shade provider that naturally repels mosquito vectors.
fun_fact: Often hailed as the 'Village Pharmacy' of India; azadirachtin from its seeds is the world's most widely used natural bio-insecticide.

light: Full sun to partial morning sun
water_notes: Water thoroughly when topsoil dries. Does not tolerate swampy, wet roots.
soil: Rich, acidic to neutral loamy soil enriched with compost and buttermilk drench.
fertilizer: Feed with sour buttermilk diluted with water (1:10) once a month; blood meal or nitrogen pellets.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic in culinary amounts
toxicity_humans: Non-toxic; daily culinary staple packed with iron and antioxidants
growth_notes: Prune main stem tip when young to promote branch branching. Protect from cold frost.
fun_fact: Not related to curry powder! Its essential oils release the unmistakable aromatic fragrance that defines South Indian tempering (tadka).

light: Partial sun to bright indirect light
water_notes: Loves consistent soil moisture. Will droop rapidly if soil dries completely.
soil: Rich, organic, moist loam with vermicompost.
fertilizer: Organic compost tea every 3 weeks.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to dogs and cats in large quantities
growth_notes: Spreads aggressively via underground runners (stolons). Plant in dedicated containers to prevent overtaking garden beds.
fun_fact: Fresh crushed pudina leaves rubbed on the skin act as a natural cooling insect repellent due to active menthol compounds.

light: Morning sun with afternoon shade in hot climates
water_notes: Keep soil evenly moist. High heat combined with dry soil triggers premature bolting (flowering).
soil: Light, fertile, fast-draining potting soil.
fertilizer: Light organic liquid seaweed fertilizer.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic and safe
growth_notes: Crush round coriander seeds gently into halves before sowing to speed up germination within 7-10 days.
fun_fact: A genetic variation in human olfactory receptor gene OR6A2 causes 10% of people to perceive coriander as tasting like harsh dish soap.

water_notes: Prefers regular watering during summer; drought tolerant once clump is established.
soil: Rich loamy soil with plenty of compost.
fertilizer: Nitrogen-rich organic manure twice a year.
toxicity_pets: Toxic to cats and dogs (citronellal causes upset)
toxicity_humans: Non-toxic; popular tea infusion and Asian culinary stalk
growth_notes: Forms dense arching clumps up to 4-5 feet tall. Easily propagated by dividing root clumps.
fun_fact: Natural source of citronella oil, extensively used worldwide to repel mosquitoes and formulate soothing aromatherapy teas.

light: Full direct sun to partial sun
water_notes: Keep seedbed consistently moist during germination and shoot growth.
soil: Well-drained loamy soil with neutral pH (6.5 - 7.5).
fertilizer: Legume that fixes its own nitrogen; modest compost is sufficient.
toxicity_pets: Safe in micro amounts; avoid raw seed excess in dogs
toxicity_humans: Non-toxic; nutritious leafy green and spice
growth_notes: One of the fastest microgreens to grow; micro-leaves can be harvested within 18-21 days of sowing.
fun_fact: Rich in 4-hydroxyisoleucine, widely studied for its ability to enhance insulin sensitivity and lower blood glucose levels.

light: Filtered partial shade; cannot tolerate scorching direct afternoon sun
water_notes: Soil must be moist but never soggy. Soggy soil rots underground rhizomes.
soil: Loose, rich, friable loam mixed with vermicompost and sand.
fertilizer: Feed with potash and compost every 4 weeks.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic in small amounts
growth_notes: Plant fresh plump grocery ginger root with visible 'eyes' (buds) facing upwards 2 inches deep.
fun_fact: Ginger is not a true root but a modified subterranean stem called a rhizome, utilized in Ayurvedic remedies for over 4,000 years.

light: Warm partial sun with afternoon shade
water_notes: Needs consistent moisture during 8-9 month growing season. Withhold water when leaves turn yellow prior to harvest.
soil: Deep, loose, fertile sandy-loam soil.
fertilizer: Heavy feeder; generous compost and organic bone meal.
toxicity_pets: Safe in culinary amounts
growth_notes: Produces stunning white and pink floral spikes beneath tropical broad green leaves.
fun_fact: Contains the golden polyphenol curcumin, world-renowned for potent natural anti-inflammatory, anticancer, and wound-healing properties.

light: Full direct sun (minimum 6 hours daily for abundant flowering)
water_notes: Water daily in summer heat; keep soil evenly moist during bloom production.
soil: Rich, porous, slightly acidic soil (pH 6.0-6.8) with compost.
fertilizer: High-potassium, low-phosphorus fertilizer every 2 weeks during peak bloom season.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic (standard rose-sinensis is pet safe)
toxicity_humans: Non-toxic; petals brewed into tart antioxidant tea
growth_notes: Prune hard in early spring to stimulate vigorous new flowering wood. Highly attractive to butterflies and sunbirds.
fun_fact: Used across South India in traditional hair care oil formulations; rich in amino acids that nourish hair follicles and prevent premature greying.

light: Full direct sun for at least 5-6 hours daily
water_notes: Water deeply when top inch of soil is dry. Reduce watering before pruning to trigger flowering flush.
soil: Rich loamy soil with well-rotted cow manure and sand.
fertilizer: Mustard cake liquid fertilizer or Epsom salts + organic compost every month.
toxicity_pets: True jasmine (Jasminum) is non-toxic to pets
toxicity_humans: Non-toxic; famous tea and garland blossom
growth_notes: Prune vigorously after each flowering cycle; flowers emerge exclusively on fresh new stem flushes.
fun_fact: The National Flower of the Philippines and revered across Madurai (India) for its unmatched, intoxicating nocturnal perfume.

water_notes: Allow soil surface to dry between waterings. Avoid wetting flower heads to prevent fungal rot.
soil: Standard garden soil with good drainage.
fertilizer: Low nitrogen fertilizer; excess nitrogen produces lush leaves with zero flowers.
toxicity_pets: Mild toxicity; can cause slight skin irritation in dogs
toxicity_humans: Non-toxic; petals used in salads and food coloring
growth_notes: Deadhead faded flowers continuously to force non-stop blooming throughout festivals and weddings.
fun_fact: Marigold roots secrete alpha-terthienyl, an organic biochemical that suppresses parasitic root-knot nematodes in companion gardens.

water_notes: Water deeply at the base. Overhead watering is the #1 cause of black spot and powdery mildew.
soil: Deep, rich, fertile loam with pH 6.5, fortified with bone meal and compost.
fertilizer: Rose food containing balanced NPK, magnesium sulfate (Epsom salt), and micronutrients every 3 weeks.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic (pet safe, watch for sharp prickles)
toxicity_humans: Non-toxic; petals used for Gulkand, rose water, and culinary confections
growth_notes: Annual pruning in autumn or late winter stimulates strong outward-facing cane growth and massive blooms.
fun_fact: Rosa damascena cultivated in Kashmir and Kannauj yields the world's most prized essential oil, pure Rose Attar.

water_notes: Drought lover! Keep on the dry side. Excess watering causes lush leaves with zero flowers.
soil: Gritty, fast-draining, slightly acidic soil.
fertilizer: High-potassium and phosphorus fertilizer once a month; avoid excess nitrogen.
toxicity_pets: Mildly toxic (sap causes mild dermatitis, sharp thorns)
growth_notes: The brilliant magenta, purple, orange, or white 'petals' are actually paper-thin modified leaves (bracts).
fun_fact: Stress-flowering plant: slightly withholding water for 10-14 days shocks the vine into bursting with hundreds of vivid blossoms.

light: Full direct sunlight (at least 6-8 hours daily)
water_notes: Deep, consistent watering at soil level. Inconsistent watering leads to fruit cracking and blossom end rot.
soil: Deep, nutrient-rich, well-draining loamy soil with compost and balanced pH (6.2-6.8).
fertilizer: Balanced fertilizer early; switch to high potassium and calcium when flowering starts.
toxicity_pets: Leaves and stems toxic to pets (solanine); ripe red fruit is non-toxic
growth_notes: Stake or cage indeterminate varieties; prune suckers to improve air circulation and concentrate energy into fruit.
fun_fact: Botanically a berry fruit, tomatoes are legally classified as vegetables in commerce since the 1893 US Supreme Court case Nix v. Hedden.

water_notes: Water when top 1-2 inches dry out. Mild water stress increases capsaicin spiciness.
soil: Warm, light, well-drained sandy loam rich in organic matter.
fertilizer: Organic compost and potassium-rich wood ash or sulfate of potash.
toxicity_pets: Capsaicin causes intense burning and digestive irritation in pets
toxicity_humans: Spicy culinary staple; wash hands thoroughly after handling
growth_notes: Pinch the main growing tip at 6 inches tall to trigger bushy branching and multiply harvest yield.
fun_fact: Birds are completely immune to the burning sensation of capsaicin because they lack the specific TRPV1 heat receptor present in mammals.

water_notes: Needs consistent moisture, especially during flowering and fruit development.
soil: Fertile, warm, well-draining loam rich in organic compost.
fertilizer: Balanced organic NPK fertilizer monthly.
toxicity_pets: Foliage contains solanine and is toxic to pets
growth_notes: Native to the Indian subcontinent where it has been cultivated for over 4,000 years with hundreds of heirloom landraces.
fun_fact: Contains the highest concentration of natural dietary nicotine of any edible plant (though you would need to eat 20 lbs to equal one cigarette!).

water_notes: Drought tolerant, but regular watering yields tender pods. Avoid waterlogging.
soil: Fertile well-drained loam with pH 6.0 to 7.5.
fertilizer: Compost and balanced organic manure during early vegetative phase.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic
growth_notes: Harvest tender young pods every 2-3 days; mature overgrown pods quickly turn tough and woody.
fun_fact: Its stunning pale yellow blossoms with deep crimson centers reveal its close taxonomic family relationship to ornamental hibiscus.

water_notes: Requires flooded puddle conditions (2-4 inches standing water) during vegetative and reproductive stages.
soil: Heavy clay loam or alluvial soils capable of retaining water.
fertilizer: Split application of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic
toxicity_humans: Primary staple food for more than half the human population
growth_notes: Paddy nursery seedlings are transplanted into puddled fields after 21-25 days.
fun_fact: India is the birthplace of aromatic Basmati rice, guarded under geographical indication across the foothills of the Himalayas.

light: Full sun throughout cool Rabi winter season
water_notes: Critical irrigation stages: Crown Root Initiation (21 days), Tillering, Flowering, and Milk stage.
soil: Well-drained fertile clay-loam soil.
fertilizer: NPK 120:60:40 kg/hectare with zinc sulfate.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic (cat grass is wheat grass!)
growth_notes: Requires cool temperatures for tillering and bright warm dry sunshine for grain filling and ripening.
fun_fact: The Green Revolution spearheaded in Punjab and Haryana transformed India from a food-scarce nation to one of the world's largest wheat exporters.

water_notes: Sensitive to both drought and waterlogging during tasseling and silking.
soil: Deep, rich, well-aerated sandy loam to silt loam.
fertilizer: High nitrogen feeder; side-dress nitrogen when knee-high.
toxicity_pets: Corn kernels safe; cobs cause dangerous intestinal blockage
growth_notes: Wind-pollinated; each individual silk strand on the cob connects to a single potential corn kernel.
fun_fact: A single ear of corn always has an even number of kernel rows (typically 16 rows and about 800 kernels).

water_notes: Deep taproot system; mature trees need water only during prolonged dry spells and fruit development.
soil: Deep, fertile alluvial or red loamy soil with excellent drainage.
fertilizer: Well-rotted farmyard manure and organic potash post-harvest in monsoon.
toxicity_pets: Fruit pulp safe; pit and sap toxic/choking hazard
toxicity_humans: Sap contains urushiol, causing dermatitis in sensitive individuals; fruit delicious
growth_notes: Needs a dry spell in winter to stimulate floral bud induction. Protect blossoms from winter frost.
fun_fact: The National Fruit of India, Pakistan, and the Philippines. India produces over 1,000 distinct varieties including Alphonso, Dasheri, and Banganapalle.

water_notes: Immense water requirement; broad foliage transpires heavily. Keep soil consistently rich and moist.
soil: Deep, rich, fertile loam with high organic matter and rapid drainage.
fertilizer: Extremely heavy potassium and nitrogen feeder; feed monthly.
toxicity_pets: 100% Non-toxic and safe
toxicity_humans: Entire plant is edible: fruit, flower blossom, inner stem, and leaves used as traditional eco-plates
growth_notes: Not a true woody tree but the world's largest perennial herbaceous plant; the 'trunk' is a pseudostem of tightly packed leaf sheaths.
fun_fact: Every part of the banana plant has a sacred role in Indian culture: leaves as dining plates, blossoms as curry, and stems for dietary fiber.

water_notes: Needs abundant water (40-50 liters daily per adult tree) with good groundwater movement.
soil: Deep coastal sandy loam or alluvial soil with high salinity tolerance.
fertilizer: Potassium chloride (common salt), neem cake, and micronutrients.
toxicity_pets: Pulp and water safe; high fat in large quantities causes upset
toxicity_humans: Pure nourishing natural electrolyte water and versatile oil/copra
growth_notes: Known in Sanskrit as 'Kalpavriksha' (the divine tree that provides all necessities of life).
fun_fact: A mature coconut palm can produce between 50 and 100 coconuts annually and can live for well over 80 to 100 years.

common_name: Banyan Tree (National Tree of India / Bargad)
water_notes: Deeply drought-tolerant once established with vast subterranean root network.
soil: Extremely hardy; can grow in rocky terrain, brick walls, and clay.
fertilizer: Self-sustaining through leaf litter compost.
toxicity_pets: Milky latex sap is mildly toxic to pets
toxicity_humans: Milky latex sap can cause eye and skin irritation
growth_notes: Sends down thick pillar-like prop roots from high horizontal branches that root into the soil, creating an entire forest from a single tree.
fun_fact: The Great Banyan Tree in Kolkata covers over 4.7 acres with more than 3,700 aerial prop roots, looking like an expansive dense forest.

water_notes: Extremely drought-tolerant. Young seedlings can survive with sparse rain.
soil: Adaptable to all soil types; can grow even out of cracked stone walls.
fertilizer: Natural organic compost.
toxicity_pets: Ficus sap mildly toxic
toxicity_humans: Non-toxic; revered medicinal bark and leaves in Ayurveda
growth_notes: Distinctive heart-shaped leaves with an elongated drip tip that flutter continuously in the faintest breeze.
fun_fact: It was meditating beneath a Sacred Peepal tree (the Bodhi Tree) in Bodh Gaya that Siddhartha Gautama attained supreme spiritual enlightenment to become the Buddha.

water_notes: Extremely sensitive to standing water and waterlogging which causes immediate stem and root rot.
soil: Rich, well-aerated, porous sandy loam with perfect drainage.
fertilizer: Monthly compost and organic potash during fruit set.
toxicity_pets: Ripe fruit safe; seeds and skin contain carpine and papain (irritant)
toxicity_humans: Fruit nutritious; green unripened skin contains high enzyme papain
growth_notes: Fast-growing single-stemmed tree that begins bearing fruit within 9 to 11 months of seed germination.
fun_fact: Papaya leaf juice is widely used in tropical medicine as a supportive natural remedy to rapidly boost blood platelet counts during dengue fever.

water_notes: Drought-tolerant once rooted; water weekly during fruit swell.
soil: Adaptable to clay, loam, or sandy soils with pH 5.0 to 7.5.
fertilizer: Organic manure and balanced NPK twice a year.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic and pet safe
toxicity_humans: Nutritious fruit containing 4x the Vitamin C of an orange
growth_notes: Smooth mottled copper bark that naturally peels; prune branches annually to encourage new fruiting shoots.
fun_fact: Guava fruit packs over 400% of your daily Vitamin C requirement in a single fruit, far surpassing oranges and lemons.

light: Full blazing sun and hot dry climate
water_notes: Drought-resistant; water regularly during fruit development to prevent fruit splitting.
soil: Well-drained light loamy or sandy soil; tolerates moderate salinity.
fertilizer: Organic compost and zinc micronutrients before flowering.
toxicity_pets: Seeds can cause minor stomach upset in dogs if eaten in large amounts
toxicity_humans: Superfood rich in punicalagins and polyphenol antioxidants
growth_notes: Shrubby multi-stemmed deciduous tree featuring fiery scarlet blossoms and ruby seed arils.
fun_fact: Maharashtra (Solapur and Nashik) is the Pomegranate capital of India, producing world-famous Bhagwa rubies exported globally.

water_notes: Water deeply when top 2 inches dry. Prone to yellowing if roots sit in standing puddle.
soil: Slightly acidic, well-draining sandy loam.
fertilizer: Citrus specific fertilizer with iron, magnesium, and zinc every 6 weeks.
toxicity_pets: Citrus oils and psoralens toxic to dogs and cats
growth_notes: Intensely fragrant white blossoms that self-pollinate; thin dense inward branches to allow sunlight into the center.
fun_fact: A staple of Indian doorsteps where lemons and green chilies (Nimbu-Mirchi) are traditionally strung together to ward off negative energy (Alakshmi).

water_notes: Hardy and drought tolerant once established; water during dry summer spells.
soil: Light to medium loam with good drainage; tolerates alkaline soils.
fertilizer: Organic cow dung compost once before monsoon.
toxicity_pets: Non-toxic
toxicity_humans: Primary ingredient in Ayurvedic Chyawanprash; supreme natural Vitamin C
growth_notes: Deciduous tree with delicate feathery light-green foliage and translucent green sour astringent fruits.
fun_fact: Amla is one of the three ingredients in Triphala, revered in Charaka Samhita as the premier Rasayana herb for longevity.

water_notes: Highly drought-resistant; roots rot quickly in stagnant water.
soil: Sandy, freely-draining, well-aerated soil.
fertilizer: Rarely needs fertilizer; modest compost annually.
toxicity_pets: Roots and bark toxic to animals; leaves safe in small amounts
toxicity_humans: Superfood leaves and drumstick pods rich in protein, iron, and calcium
growth_notes: Super fast grower; can shoot up 10-15 feet in its very first year from seed.
fun_fact: Gram for gram, moringa leaves contain 7 times more Vitamin C than oranges, 4 times more Vitamin A than carrots, and 4 times more calcium than milk.

water_notes: Water every 7 days or when the top 1-2 inches of soil feel dry.
soil: Well-draining rich garden soil enriched with organic matter.
fertilizer: Balanced organic fertilizer every 4 weeks in active growth season.
toxicity_pets: Mild toxicity; keep away from curious pets
growth_notes: White pinstripe variegation
fun_fact: A celebrated species of the Araceae family, widely cultivated across diverse climatic zones.

water_notes: Water every 6 days or when the top 1-2 inches of soil feel dry.
soil: Well-draining rich garden soil enriched with organic matter.
fertilizer: Balanced organic fertilizer every 4 weeks in active growth season.
toxicity_pets: Mild toxicity; keep away from curious pets
growth_notes: Trailing heart-shaped foliage
fun_fact: A celebrated species of the Araceae family, widely cultivated across diverse climatic zones.

water_notes: Water every 12 days or when the top 1-2 inches of soil feel dry.
soil: Well-draining rich garden soil enriched with organic matter.
fertilizer: Balanced organic fertilizer every 4 weeks in active growth season.
toxicity_pets: Mild toxicity; keep away from curious pets
growth_notes: Indestructible dark-green leaves
fun_fact: A celebrated species of the Asparagaceae family, widely cultivated across diverse climatic zones.

water_notes: Water every 6 days or when the top 1-2 inches of soil feel dry.
soil: Well-draining rich garden soil enriched with organic matter.
fertilizer: Balanced organic fertilizer every 4 weeks in active growth season.
toxicity_pets: Mild toxicity; keep away from curious pets
growth_notes: Round saucer pancake leaves
fun_fact: A celebrated species of the Urticaceae family, widely cultivated across diverse climatic zones.

water_notes: Water every 12 days or when the top 1-2 inches of soil feel dry.
soil: Well-draining rich garden soil enriched with organic matter.
fertilizer: Balanced organic fertilizer every 4 weeks in active growth season.
toxicity_pets: Mild toxicity; keep away from curious pets
